paper_citations.target_scenario: DASH-based real-time point cloud video streaming; Sec.III.A System Overview p.3 (PDF page numbering in extract)
paper_citations.topology: Client-server (C/S) architecture; server prepares chunks; client downloads tiles (Sec.III.A; Fig.1 Architecture p.4 / IEEE p.7873)
paper_citations.transport: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH) over HTTP/TCP (Abstract/Intro; Sec.III.A)
paper_citations.delivery_semantics: Per-client HTTP download requests of selected tile representations; unicast request-response (Fig.1 p.4)
paper_citations.independent_stream: Yes — client issues download request for optimal representation of GoF k (Fig.1; Sec.III.A)
paper_citations.cross_user_fanout: Not described; C/S DASH per client
paper_citations.shared_representation_decision: No multi-user grouping; decisions are per-stream POT/DRL for that client session
paper_citations.controller_placement: Client-side rolling POT + DRL solver; decision sent as download request to server (Fig.1 p.4)
paper_citations.adaptation_inputs: Predicted bandwidth and FoV; buffer state; QoE model Eq.1–8 (Sec.III.B p.4–5)
paper_citations.content_unit: Tiles within Groups of Frames (GoFs); quality levels l (Eq.2 p.4)
paper_citations.buffering: Playback buffer bf with constraints (Eq.9c; Theorem 1 buffer stability p.6)
paper_citations.quality_bitrate: Select tile quality levels via binary x_k,c,l (P1/P2)
paper_citations.prediction_horizon: Rolling window of N GoFs (Sec.III.A; P2 p.6)
paper_citations.optimization_drl: SC-DDQN / DRL solver for real-time POT (paper V.B & evaluation)
paper_citations.limitations_vs_our_media: Mapped onto layered Rep ladder + SC-DDQN weights in DASH/Rolling
